USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

Late joint complications of fractures: 2

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient’s fracture has united, but the adjacent joint repeatedly gives way during activity. Examination identifies residual ligament insufficiency rather than fixed loss of movement. Which late functional complication best describes this problem?

  1. Osteonecrosis
  2. Nonunion
  3. Post-traumatic osteoarthritis
  4. Joint instability
  5. Joint stiffness
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Joint instability

Ligament insufficiency or altered bony support can cause giving way and abnormal joint motion.

Understanding the options

Joint instability
Ligament insufficiency or altered bony support can cause giving way and abnormal joint motion.
Joint stiffness
Capsular contracture, adhesions and prolonged immobilization can restrict motion after injury. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Osteonecrosis
Disruption of blood supply can lead to death and collapse of an injured bony segment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Nonunion
Persistent failure of fracture healing requires assessment of stability, biology, infection and patient factors. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Post-traumatic osteoarthritis
Articular incongruity or cartilage damage can cause later degenerative joint changes. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
